en: Book I · Leaving home to seek the way
zh: 第一卷 · 弃家求道

en: Mist lies on the great river. At the stern of the raft a white-haired ferryman stands, his pole set in the water, in no haste to push—he is listening.
zh: 大河上起着薄雾。筏尾立着一个白发的撑船人，篙子插在水里，却不急着推——他在听。

en: In the sound of the water there is everything: the cry of market-goers, cattle stepping into the shallows, a child's night-wailing far away, and the breath a boy let out at last, after standing the whole night through, when day broke. A thousand voices mingle, and at the end they become one sound, low and steady, as if the earth itself were humming.
zh: 水声里什么都有：赶集人的吆喝，牛蹄踏进浅滩，远处婴儿的夜啼，还有一个少年站了整整一夜、天亮时才吐出来的那口气。千百种声音搅在一处，末了并成一个又低又稳的音，像大地自己在哼。

en: What the ferryman hears is his own life. And that life must be told from far off—from two thousand five hundred years ago, from a Brahmin courtyard upstream on this same river.
zh: 撑船人听见的，是他自己的一辈子。而这一辈子，要从很远的地方讲起——从两千五百年前，从这条河上游的一座婆罗门院子讲起。

en: In that courtyard the shadow of the fig tree moved each day from the east wall to the west. The boy who grew there could recite every scripture, and at the river he could complete the whole rite of bathing and sacrifice. The elders said he would be a priest among priests.
zh: 那院子里的无花果树影，每天从东墙挪到西墙。院里长大的少年会背诵所有的经文，会在河边做完整套沐浴与献祭。长者们说，他将来会是祭司中的祭司。

en: Only he himself was unquiet: in the scriptures, in the offerings, in his father's speech, he could not find the Self he sought.
zh: 只有他自己不安：经文里、供奉里、父亲的言语里，都没有他要找的那个「我」。

en: One evening in the rains, three Samanas passed the village gate. Dust showed their lean shoulder-blades; their eyes were unnaturally bright. They left not a word behind.
zh: 一个雨季的黄昏，三个沙门走过村口。尘土里露出他们瘦削的肩胛，眼睛亮得反常，一句话也没有留下。

en: That night the boy stood before his father's door, and did not move. He stood the whole night through. At daybreak his father let him go.
zh: 那天夜里，少年站到父亲的门前，一动不动。他站了整整一夜，天亮时父亲让他走。

en: Book II · Samsara
zh: 第二卷 · 尘世轮回

en: Three years in the forest of the Samanas taught him fasting, the bearing of pain, and how to send himself out of the body. Hunger could only press that Self smaller; it never dissolved it.
zh: 苦修林里的三年，他学会了斋戒、忍痛、把自己从身体里放出去。可饥饿只能把那个「我」压小，从来没有把它化开。

en: With his companion he went to Jetavana to hear the Perfect One teach. When it was done he bowed to that man, and left alone—doctrine can be given; awakening cannot.
zh: 他和同伴一起去祇园精舍听那位圆满者说法。听完，他向那人行礼，然后独自离开——道理可以传授，觉悟不能。

en: Beyond the river lay a great city: silks, spices, dice, a courtesan's garden, and a merchant house still growing. First he learned to write and keep accounts; then wine, and love.
zh: 过河之后是一座繁华大城：绸缎、香料、骰子、名妓的园子，和一个正在扩张的商号。他先学会了写字算账，再学会了饮酒与情爱。

en: Twenty years passed. He had a house, servants, a room of fine clothes—and new cares: fear of defeat, of age, of losing what he had. Year by year the face in the mirror grew softer.
zh: 二十年过去，他有了宅第、仆人和一屋子华服，也有了新的心事：怕输、怕老、怕失去。镜子里的脸一年年软下去。

en: One morning he left the house and the ledgers and walked toward the river. Only at the water did he find that the voice in his breast had been silent a long time.
zh: 一个清晨，他丢下宅子与账簿往河边走。走到水边才发现，胸口那个声音已经很久没有响过了。

en: Book III · The river made whole
zh: 第三卷 · 河水圆融

en: He came back to the ferry that had once carried him across. The ferryman Vasudeva was still there. He knew him, and asked nothing more.
zh: 他回到当年渡他过河的渡口。那位船夫维稣德瓦还在，认出了他，也没有多问一句。

en: He poled with the ferryman, braided rope, mended oars, and learned to listen to the water. Year by year the river said more: it was at the source, at the crossing, and at the sea's mouth, all at once, and never in haste.
zh: 他跟着船夫撑船、编绳、修桨，学着听水声。河水一年比一年说得多：它同时在源头、在渡口、在入海口，从不着急。

en: Many years later the city's courtesan Kamala came to the ferry with a child, and was bitten by a snake on the bank. She died in the hut. The child remained.
zh: 许多年后，城里的名妓伽摩拉带着一个孩子来渡河，在岸边被蛇咬了。她死在草舍里，孩子留了下来。

en: The boy hated the river, and hated this father who had appeared so suddenly. He would not pole; he would not eat coarse food. One night he took the money and fled toward the city.
zh: 那孩子恨这条河，也恨这个忽然出现的父亲。他不肯撑船，不肯吃粗饭，某个夜里带着钱往城里逃了。

en: Halfway in the chase, Siddhartha saw a face in the water—his father's face, and his own. He turned back to the ferry.
zh: 追到半路，悉达多在水面上看见一张脸——那是他父亲的脸，也是他自己的。他掉头回了渡口。

en: Epilogue · The ferry
zh: 尾声 · 渡口

en: The ferryman Vasudeva put the oar into his hands, walked into the woods, and did not come back.
zh: 船夫维稣德瓦把桨交给他，走进林子里，再没有回来。

en: He kept the ferry alone, and carried people across. Some went to market, some to a burial, some only to look once upon a daughter; the river asked nothing.
zh: 他一个人守着渡口，替人渡河。有人赶集，有人奔丧，有人只是过河去看一眼女儿；河水一句也不多问。

en: Many years passed. An old friend with white hair, Govinda, came to the ferry. He had sought a lifetime and was still seeking; at first he did not know the man at the pole.
zh: 很多年过去，一位白发的老友侨文达来到渡口。他找了一辈子，仍然在找，起先并没有认出撑船的人是谁。

en: Siddhartha bade him look down at the water. Upon it rose a thousand thousand faces: child, old man, fish, the dying, the newborn, flowing away together and flowing back.
zh: 悉达多让他低头看水面。水面上浮起千万张脸：孩子、老人、鱼、垂死的人、初生的人，一起流过去，又一起流回来。

en: The old friend kissed his brow. Tears fell on the boards of the boat, and he himself could not say why.
zh: 老友吻了他的额头，泪水落在船板上，自己也说不清是为什么。

en: “He smiled, no different from a thousand thousand others.”
zh: 「他微笑着，与千万人一般无二。」

en: The next day people still stepped on and off at the ferry. The groove worn by the rope in the post was a little deeper.
zh: 第二天渡口照旧有人上船、下船。木桩上被缆绳磨出的凹痕又深了一点。

en: The city on the bank went on trading; in the forest of the Samanas men still fasted; at Jetavana they still taught; the river still went toward the sea.
zh: 岸上的城市继续做生意，苦修林里继续有人斋戒，祇园里继续有人说法，河水继续往海里去。

en: (Adapted from Hermann Hesse's Siddhartha.)
zh: （改编自赫尔曼·黑塞《悉达多》。）

en: Siddhartha · The Ferryman — after the novel by Hermann Hesse
zh: 悉达多 · 渡河人 —— 根据赫尔曼·黑塞同名小说改编
